verdicts.evidence: $ is redundant after a greedy (.+): in JS the dot excludes line terminators (\n AND \r), so (.+) extends exactly to the position where multiline $ always succeeds — no backtracking possible, identical acceptance and capture on every string. Sensitivity control: the candidate inputs for divergence are end of file without \n, CRLF (capture before \r) and trailing whitespace (captured by both forms then trimmed) — measured identical on the trail and CRLF fixtures, by function AND by check --strict (cli-trail, cli-crlf: outputs and exit codes byte for byte identical).

verdicts.evidence: The signature is a regex SOURCE (ADR-0020): an untrimmed trailing whitespace becomes a literal space required in the proof. RECIPE: example mission, frontier-deterministic-boundary.md (signed rule, applied row of floor.md) carries "signature: guardFields" with ONE trailing space — guardFields exists in guard.ts but always followed by "(", never by a space; lock re-signed. MEASURED: shipped → trim, /guardFields/i matches, exit 0; mutated → "evidence does not match the rule's signature /guardFields /i", exit 1 — the shape check renders a false verdict on a compliant proof, and symmetrically the "rest on a signed rule" count gets distorted. CRLF measured identical (\r excluded from the capture by JS `.`/`$`): the remaining door is in-line whitespace, absent from every shipped corpus (grep checked).

verdicts.evidence: Same recipe as the \s twin ("signature:zzqx9" without a space, pattern absent from the proof), different mechanics: the greedy \S* swallows the value and backtracking leaves the last character to (.+) — the signature becomes "9". MEASURED: shipped → violation "/zzqx9/i", exit 1; mutated → /9/i matches the cited test file (7 occurrences of "9"), verdict GREEN, exit 0. A shape check reduced to the last character of its regex matches roughly any proof: red→green measured, the gate validates in shape what it should have refused. On the normal form with a space, \S* matches empty and nothing moves — which is why the whole shipped corpus (a space every time, grep checked) leaves the mutant invisible.
